rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, ending a tenancy, or charging a higher deposit or rent based on criminal history. Where an exception allows action based on criminal history, the landlord must give the applicant or tenant written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.key_value: Prohibits criminal-history inquiries and use in rental housing decisions
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.coverage_text: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, with regard to current or prospective tenants.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing and Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as a primary residence; units under a rental agreement letting owners move back in per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add or replace roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation. Civil damages, including actual damages or three times one month's rent. Punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.extraction_note: This is the Rent Board summary page, not the ordinance text. The page states that City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; no effective date is given. Status of in_force is inferred from the page describing current enforcement and complaint procedures. Landlords must also post a Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants.
